clue.text: Can Russia's assembly revoke independence to protect energy guarantees?

indicators.note: to protect is to surround and shield, so the shuffled letters wrap round the energy letter
an assembly puts parts together, so the letters of the two words are put together in a new order
to revoke is to withdraw, so one letter is taken away from the fodder

parts.note: the possessive S counts here as a letter of the fodder
I is the usual abbreviation for independence or independent
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A question about whether a Russian parliament might cancel a country's independence while shielding its energy supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revoke' takes I from CANRUSSIAS; 'assembly' rearranges the rest, and 'to protect' puts E inside near the end. The possessive S of Russia's is needed as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Assurances are firm promises or pledges, which is what guarantees are; the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Sponge recipe accepted by sailor, not drunk

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the crossword sailor

indicators.note: being accepted by means being taken inside, so the recipe letter goes into the word for sober

parts.note: someone not drunk is sober
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from the Latin 'take' on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A cake recipe being handed to a sailor who happens to be sober.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sponge' looks like a cake to go with the recipe, but it is the definition: something that soaks things up. R for recipe is the old prescription abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponge soaks up liquid, so it is something that absorbs: a straightforward example.

clue.text: Reason isn't a substitute to ask "why?"

indicators.note: substitute is read as a verb, swapping the letters of these words around into a new order
to ask is to speak a question, so the word why is heard rather than written, giving a single letter

parts.note: the question word why is spoken the same as the letter Y

explanation.surface: Someone claiming that rational thought cannot replace simply asking why.
explanation.walkthrough: 'substitute' rearranges ISNTA into SANIT; 'ask' means say the word why, which gives the letter Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Reason as a noun can mean soundness of mind, as in 'losing one's reason', which is a synonym.

clue.text: Priestess consumed by large, northern animal

indicators.note: being consumed by means being swallowed inside, so the priestess goes inside the other two letters

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
Io, in Greek myth, was a priestess of Hera loved by Zeus

explanation.surface: A priestess being eaten by a big creature from the north, like an old sacrificial legend.
explanation.walkthrough: Io is a classical figure: a priestess of Hera whom Zeus turned into a heifer.
explanation.definitionFit: The lion is a big cat, so it is one example of an animal.

clue.text: Without consideration, no matter what

definitions.meaning: having no regard, careless of others or of the consequences
anyway, despite everything, as in 'carry on whatever happens'

explanation.surface: Two ways of saying something will be done heedlessly and come what may.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense can also be seen as REGARD (consideration) plus LESS (without).
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both heedless of others and, as an adverb, nevertheless or in any event.

clue.text: He gets near battle

indicators.note: battle suggests a struggle or mêlée, so the letters of the two words before it fight their way into a new order

explanation.surface: A man who goes towards the fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battle' rearranges GETS NEAR; read whole, the clue describes an army NCO who goes close to combat.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-commissioned army officer is a soldier who goes close to the fighting, so the whole clue describes him.

clue.text: Ball keeping low loses golf games

indicators.note: to lose something is to be left without it, so one letter drops out of the word

parts.note: a grubber is a kick or ball in rugby or cricket that runs low along the ground
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A sports report: a low-kept ball causes golf games to be lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' takes G from GRUBBER, a rugby kick that skims along the ground. A rubber in bridge or whist is a set of games, usually best of three.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge and whist a rubber is a match made up of a series of games, so the plural fits.

clue.text: Eat crackers after strong cheese

indicators.note: after places the scrambled word behind the letter for strong

parts.note: F stands for forte, the musical direction meaning loud or strong

indicators.note: crackers means crazy, so the letters of eat are scrambled

explanation.surface: An instruction to eat crackers following a strong cheese, like a cheeseboard tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crackers' looks like the biscuits to go with cheese, but it rearranges EAT into ETA.
explanation.definitionFit: Feta is a crumbly white Greek cheese made from sheep's milk, so it is an example.

clue.text: Stand by, I'm near plastic vessel

parts.note: a sub, or substitute, is a stand-by player

indicators.note: plastic means mouldable, so the letters can be reshaped into a different word

explanation.surface: A worried sailor near a plastic boat being told to wait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plastic' looks like the boat's material, but it rearranges IMNEAR into MARINE.
explanation.definitionFit: An underwater craft is a kind of vessel, so the definition is a broad category.

clue.text: Puzzle introduction needs no PR

indicators.note: needs no means does without, so the two letters are taken off the word for introduction

parts.note: a prelude is an introductory piece or opening

explanation.surface: A publicist's boast that a puzzle needs no introduction and no promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs no' removes PR from PRELUDE. 'Puzzle' is a verb here: to baffle, to escape someone's grasp.
explanation.definitionFit: If something puzzles you it escapes your understanding, as in 'the answer escaped me': a synonym sense.

clue.text: University principal's first article is ideal

parts.note: principal as an adjective means chief, top
I is the Roman numeral one, hence first
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A university head's opening essay being called perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'principal' looks like a college head, but here it is the adjective meaning chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ideal is perfect in a dreamlike, unrealistic way, like a perfect imagined society.

clue.text: Subject's gradable problem? D minus

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the definition reads 'the subject is'

indicators.note: a problem is something to work out, so the letters of gradable are worked into a new order
minus means one letter of the fodder is left over and not used in the new word

explanation.surface: A student complaining that a gradable subject is a problem, earning a D minus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problem' rearranges GRADABLE, and 'D minus' says the D is left out: the remaining seven letters make the answer. 'D minus' looks like a poor mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Algebra is a branch of mathematics, a school subject: the answer is one example of a subject.

clue.text: Church and evangelical youth leaders welcome bishops

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the first letters wrap round the bishops
leaders are the front runners, so take the opening letter of each of the three words

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for a bishop, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A church and its young evangelical leaders greeting visiting bishops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' takes A, E and Y from and, evangelical, youth; 'welcome' puts BB (two bishops) inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbey is a church belonging to a monastery, such as Westminster's, so it is an example.

clue.text: I heard dancing about the finale of Fred and Ginger

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters

indicators.note: a finale is the end, so take the closing letter of the name
dancing sets the letters moving into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone hearing gossip on the dance floor about how Fred Astaire and Ginger Rogers ended their routine.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (about) and D (end of Fred) come first, then 'dancing' rearranges I HEARD into HAIRED. Fred Astaire and Ginger Rogers were a famous dance partnership.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginger as an adjective describes orange-red hair, so a ginger person has hair of that colour.

clue.text: Actor's fury? Parts with bad unpredictability

indicators.note: to part with something is to give it up, so these three letters leave the combined words, scattered in order

parts.note: Marlon Brando, the American film actor
madness here means rage or fury

explanation.surface: A question about an actor's rage, followed by a critic noting the bad roles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parts with' removes B, A and D scattered through BRANDOMADNESS (the first B, then the second A and D), leaving the answer. 'Parts' looks like acting roles.
explanation.definitionFit: Unpredictability is the quality of being haphazard and without pattern, a close synonym.

clue.text: Covers performances about good man and woman

indicators.note: about means around, so the words for performances wrap round the other pieces

parts.note: duets are performances by two people
ST, saint, is the crossword good man
she is the pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A review of shows centred on a virtuous man and a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the good man (a saint) and the woman inside the performances. 'Covers' looks like cover versions of songs, but it is a plural noun for protective cloths.
explanation.definitionFit: Dust sheets are cloths laid over furniture to protect it, so they are things that cover.

clue.text: Her rebukes in bed regarding the drapes?

definitions.text: Her rebukes in bed regarding the drapes?

parts.words: Her rebukes in bed regarding the drapes?
parts.note: a wife's private scolding of her husband, given in bed with the bed-curtains drawn, could jokingly be a talk about the curtains

explanation.surface: A woman scolding her partner in bed about the choice of curtains.
explanation.walkthrough: The old term means a private reproof given by a wife in bed, in the days of four-poster beds hung with curtains; the second half pretends it is a talk on soft furnishings.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a dated idiom for a wife's reproof of her husband in private, at night.

clue.text: Process dictates rigorous appraisal

indicators.note: to process is to treat or work over, so the letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A description of how a strict evaluation is carried out, as if procedure dictated it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Process' is read as a verb telling you to work over the letters of 'dictates'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from testing gold with nitric acid; it now means any decisive, searching test.

clue.text: Minister's mistress raises gun: …

indicators.note: in a down answer, raising a word means writing it from the bottom upwards, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a vicar's lover, REV (reverend, a minister) plus LOVER

explanation.surface: A melodrama: the clergyman's secret lover pulls a pistol.
explanation.walkthrough: REV is the short form of Reverend, a minister's title; the minister's mistress is his lover, so REV LOVER. The ellipsis leads on to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A revolver is a pistol with a rotating cylinder, so it is one kind of gun.

clue.text: Clergy with their heads in the clouds?

definitions.text: Clergy with their heads in the clouds?

parts.words: Clergy with their heads in the clouds?
parts.note: slang for chaplains, especially service chaplains, who in the cryptic picture are aviators steering among the clouds

explanation.surface: Dreamy, unworldly churchmen with their heads in the clouds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clergy' is a plain definition and the rest a joke: the slang term pictures priests as pilots of the heavens.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang phrase means chaplains or clergymen, especially those serving with the armed forces.

clue.text: … "It's cowardly to cry over wife"

parts.note: to yell is to cry out
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Continuing the melodrama: the gunman sneers that weeping over one's wife is spineless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' looks like part of 'cry over', but it gives O. The ellipsis joins this to the previous clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is a colloquial word for lacking courage, so it is a synonym for cowardly.

clue.text: With little money, save Scrabble tiles

parts.note: P, penny, is a small amount of British money

indicators.note: to scrabble is to scrape about, so the letters of the word are jumbled

explanation.surface: Saving up a few pennies for Scrabble tiles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrabble' looks like the board game's tiles, but it rearranges SAVE into AVES. 'tiles' is a verb, as in laying a floor.
explanation.definitionFit: To pave a path is to lay a surface of slabs over it, which is what tiling does: a verb synonym.

clue.text: Look over pressure with power shower

indicators.note: over means covering, so the word for look goes round the two letters

parts.note: to peer is to look closely
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Checking the water pressure on a power shower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shower' is a verb: to pepper with shot or questions is to shower with them.
explanation.definitionFit: To pepper someone with questions or pellets is to rain many of them on that person, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Lots? No, one wave

indicators.note: to wave is to move to and fro, so the letters are swung round into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone correcting a claim of many waves: there is just the one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wave' rearranges LOTS, NO and I; read whole, the clue describes the single, solitary wave of physics.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics this is a solitary wave that keeps its shape as it travels, so 'not lots but one wave' fits.

clue.text: Immortal music?

definitions.meaning: as a noun, the undying spiritual part of a person
a genre of black American popular music, from rhythm and blues and gospel

explanation.surface: A question whether some music is everlasting.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the everlasting spirit of a person and a style of popular music.

clue.text: Back up to enter river, otherwise drive back

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river

indicators.note: to enter is to go into, so the turned word goes inside the other letters

parts.note: else means otherwise

indicators.note: back means backwards, so the little word is turned round

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions for a boat trip that ends up being forced back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns the little word round and 'to enter' puts it inside the river letter plus 'otherwise', after their first two letters. 'Back up' looks like a phrase meaning support.
explanation.definitionFit: To repulse an enemy attack is to drive it back, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Children's author's first to abandon Latin course

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving behind, so the letter for Latin is taken out of the name

parts.note: Roald, the first name of children's author Roald Dahl

explanation.surface: A children's writer being first to drop Latin from the syllabus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' looks like 'first to do something', but it means the author's first name. 'course' is a route, not a school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A road is a route or way, and course can mean a line of travel: a synonym.

clue.text: Noodles sound fishy

indicators.note: fishy means suspicious or wrong, so the letters of the word are not in their proper order

explanation.surface: Someone sniffing a bowl of noodles that seems off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like a verb meaning seem, but it is the fodder, and 'fishy' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: These are thick Japanese wheat-flour strips used in soups, so they are a kind of noodle.

clue.text: Report from small gallery: "Oh no! Monet's been vandalised"

parts.note: the Tate is the famous London art gallery

indicators.note: something vandalised has been damaged and broken up, so the remaining letters are jumbled
no here means without, so the letter for Oh is dropped from the painter's name

parts.note: Claude Monet, the French Impressionist painter; the possessive adds no letter
the exclamation oh is the letter O

explanation.surface: A news item from a gallery: a horrified cry as a Monet is defaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oh no!' looks like an exclamation, but 'no' removes O from MONET; 'been vandalised' then rearranges MNET into MENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement is a formal account of facts, and a report is the same thing: a synonym.
